Reporter Centific_IT_EMA.FA   
Status pending  

Summary 0045194: Mail Smart Replies - GROUNDEDNESS
Description hello, I read the guides regarding Smart Mail Replies and watched the update video but, to be completely honest, I am more confused than before on at least two aspects inherent to GROUNDEDNESS:

FIRST AGONIZING DOUBT

RULE 6, PAGE 32

: If the model expands the prompt with creative new information that reasonably fits in the context, it is Grounded
• If the prompt specifically asked for detailed information, it is grounded for the draft to create new info accordingly
• .For example, the prompt says, "Expand this short reply into a complete email: Here is my availability. Model may
provide hallucinate details for the availability.

Is this telling me that if there is an input email like: "Hi Maria, can you confirm you are coming to the event?"
and the prompt is something like "Expand this short reply into a complete email: Confirm that I will come"

and the generated response is: "Sure, I will be there around 9:00 PM"

Should I confirm that the response is Grounded despite the obvious hallucination (9:00 PM)?

SECOND AGONIZING DOUBT

RULE5, PAGE 31

: Recipient name should be established in the prompt or previous email (if any)
• The recipient name in a response would be considered grounded if you can identify it in the prompt or the previous
email.
• This means that if the user profile shows different names in the Address Forms field, prioritize the prompt and the
previous email, since the user profile shows a tendency and you may not be able to confirm if the names in the Address
Form field refers to the actual recipient.

In the update video, however, it says to mark it as Grounded even if the recipient's name included in the generated response is taken from the User Profiles (Addressed Forms field) and does not match the one present in the input email. What am I missing? What is meant by "prioritize"?

Now I am so confused that I don't think I will continue working on this task

Isaac Lighthouse Applicable Language(s) All
Prompt (copy full text; for VCG, please upload screenshot) 
Response (copy full text; for VCG, please upload screenshot) 
Centific's take 
Resolution 
Status' 
Upload a screnshot below and confirm "Yes" Yes
URL n/a

 Activities

 Centific_IT_EMA.FA

 2026-06-05 02:03

translator   ~0080983

 I apologize, I hadn't finished watching the video yet. I only just noticed that these specific points are actually addressed. Regarding Rule 6, I seem to understand that, in my example, I should therefore confirm that the response is Grounded. Regarding Rule 5, however, I still have some doubts: if in the input email the writer signs off as "Mark", in the User Profile we find "John", and the generated response uses the name "John" (therefore prioritizing neither the prompt nor the input email), what kind of rating should I give?

 Nenad.Vranic

 2026-06-05 03:57    private

administrator   ~0080993

 It would still be grounded. Prioritized means that in situations where you have two names mismatched (e.g. in previous email and profile), the expectation is that the previous email name should be prioritized as the expected one for the model to use. It fits groundedness as it's found within the context of the task, but it might fail contextual fit since it's not prioritizing the expected name.

 Centific_IT_EMA.FA

 2026-06-05 04:27

translator   ~0080996

 Hi Nenad, thanks again for your reply. So can I consider your first message here https://globalquery.oneforma.com/view.php?id=43647 as no longer relevant? I apologize if I keep asking questions that probably seem silly, but I find this aspect of the task very confusing :)

 Centific_IT_EMA.FA

 2026-06-05 04:38

translator   ~0080997

 Last edited: 2026-06-05 04:53

View 2 revisions

 This is an example that leaves me quite perplexed:

Source email: Hi John, I'm leaving for London today. Regards, Mark

Prompt: expand this message into a full email "when are you coming back?"

Generated response: "Hi John, have fun and don't cause too much trouble! When will you be back? Regards, Mark"

User profile: address form-> John, signature-> Mark

In an example like this (and I've come across several!), everything is extremely confusing and contradictory. Both the writer of the input email and the end user sign as Mark and address the other as John.

Looking at the User Profile, it can be deduced that it is the end user who is (or should be) named Mark. So what I would EXPECT is for the names to be reversed in the generated email.

In a case like this, should I pass it as Grounded because the names in the response (author: Mark, recipient: John) are still present in the User Profile, despite the result being paradoxical in relation to the input email, and then penalize the Contextual Fit?

 Nenad.Vranic

 2026-06-05 05:18    private

administrator   ~0081001

 That ticket was quite a while ago, since then they confirmed that it's grounded as long as it's found within the context of instructions, previous email or profile.
I would say that, since the name is not explicitly mentioned in the prompt, the previous email becomes the 'target' for names. Since the model follows the profile, it's grounded but it cannot be considered fully contextually fit.
These mix-matches may be an error on the client side, so i'd report them as a problem in the tool for the engineers awareness.

 2026-06-06 03:47

translator   ~0081040

 Thanks Nenad, I was losing my mind :)
